c.tagline: Highland capital blending German heritage and African soul.

taxi.fareNote: Fares are usually negotiated in advance rather than metered; look for taxis with visible permit discs.

emergency.note: Or dial 112 from any mobile phone for all emergencies; response times can be slow outside central areas.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Petty crime; caution in Katutura and at night

hood_desc: Leafy, upscale suburb east of downtown with tree-lined streets, boutique guesthouses and good restaurants; suits travelers who want comfort and easy taxi access to the center without downtown noise.
Quiet residential suburb near Eros Airport with B&Bs and guesthouses; suits business travelers and those wanting a calm, secure base close to embassies and the small domestic airfield.

The compact downtown core along Independence Avenue with shops, museums, craft markets and nightlife; suits first-timers and budget travelers who want to walk to sights, though extra caution is advised after dark.
Exclusive, garden-filled suburb north of the center with spacious walled guesthouses; suits travelers seeking a peaceful, upmarket retreat close to the Grove Mall of Namibia.
Elevated, historic suburb of colonial-era homes overlooking the CBD; suits travelers who want walkable proximity to downtown paired with quieter, scenic streets.

water.note: Windhoek's tap water is highly treated and considered among the safest in Africa to drink straight from the tap.

transit.pay: City bus fares are paid in cash to the driver; there is no rechargeable transit card. Shared minibus taxis (the most common local option) are paid in cash per route, agreed informally at pickup.
transit.hours: City buses run roughly 6am-7pm on weekdays with limited weekend service; there is no late-night public transit, so taxis or pre-booked transfers are needed after dark.
transit.note: Windhoek has no passenger metro or tram; most visitors rely on rental cars, hotel shuttles, or licensed taxis rather than public transit.

train: TransNamib passenger rail (limited service, e.g. Windhoek–Walvis Bay overnight train)

tip.r: A 10% tip at sit-down restaurants is appreciated but not obligatory; rounding up for taxis and porters is common.

food.name: Game meat steak
food.desc: Oryx, kudu, springbok and eland steaks, lean and faintly sweet, grilled rare and served with pap or roast potatoes.

places.name: Joe's Beerhouse
places.note: Windhoek institution since 1991; the city's best-known game grill under a roof of collected oddities.

places.name: The Stellenbosch Wine Bar & Bistro
places.note: Smart bistro pairing game cuts with a deep South African wine list.

places.name: Leo's at the Castle
places.note: Fine-dining game menu in a hilltop castle with views over the whole city.

food.name: Kapana
food.desc: Street beef sliced thin, flash-grilled over open coals and eaten standing up with chilli salt and fatcakes.

places.name: Single Quarters Kapana Market
places.note: The original kapana market; pick your cut off the grill and pay per handful.

places.name: Oshetu Community Market
places.note: Busy covered market with rows of grills, best in the late afternoon.

places.name: Eveline Street
places.note: Windhoek's nightlife strip, lined with braai stands and bars from early evening.

food.name: Potjiekos
food.desc: A slow three-legged-pot stew layered with meat, root vegetables and beer, never stirred, simmered for hours over coals.

places.name: Joe's Beerhouse
places.note: Its game potjie uses oryx and warthog when available - the signature slow-cooked order.

places.name: Xwama Traditional Restaurant
places.note: Authentic Namibian kitchen in the heart of Katutura, strong on traditional stews.

places.name: Craft Cafe
places.note: Relaxed lunch spot upstairs in the craft centre, good for home-style Namibian cooking.

food.name: Vetkoek
food.desc: Deep-fried dough puffs, crisp outside and steamy inside, split and filled with savoury mince or eaten with jam.

places.name: Craft Cafe
places.note: Easy central spot to try fatcakes with coffee without leaving the tourist core.

places.name: Xwama Traditional Restaurant
places.note: Serves vetkoek alongside the full range of Namibian home cooking.

places.name: Single Quarters Kapana Market
places.note: Fatcake stalls sit right beside the grills - the standard kapana side order.

food.name: Oshiwambo traditional plate
food.desc: Oshifima (mahangu millet pap) with beef or goat stew, wild spinach and often mopane worms - northern Namibia's staple meal.

places.name: Xwama Traditional Restaurant
places.note: The best-known address for Oshiwambo cooking, with colourful decor and cultural artefacts.

places.name: Pepata
places.note: Oshiwambo and Namibian home-style dishes in a comfortable, welcoming room.

places.name: Oshetu Community Market
places.note: Cooked-food stalls serving pap, stew and greens to market traders all day.

food.name: Walvis Bay oysters and seafood
food.desc: Cold-current Atlantic oysters trucked up from Walvis Bay, plus kingklip and hake - Namibia's coastal larder inland.

places.name: NICE Restaurant
places.note: Namibian Institute of Culinary Education training restaurant; ambitious plating of coastal seafood.

places.name: The Stellenbosch Wine Bar & Bistro
places.note: Reliable oyster and white-wine stop in the city's smartest eating district.

places.name: Leo's at the Castle
places.note: Fine-dining seafood courses with the city's best terrace view.

food.name: Windhoek Lager
food.desc: Brewed to the German purity law by Namibia Breweries since 1920; crisp, light and the national default beer.

places.name: Joe's Beerhouse
places.note: Cold draught by the litre in the city's most famous beer garden.

places.name: Sky Bar, Hilton Windhoek
places.note: Rooftop pool bar for a cold lager with a panorama of the city bowl.

places.name: The Stellenbosch Wine Bar & Bistro
places.note: Local draught alongside a serious wine list in a leafy courtyard.

food.name: Oshikundu
food.desc: Lightly fermented, faintly sour mahangu-and-sorghum drink from the north; low in alcohol and traditionally home-brewed.

places.name: Xwama Traditional Restaurant
places.note: One of the few sit-down restaurants that reliably serves traditional oshikundu.

places.name: Oshetu Community Market
places.note: Sold by the cup from market stalls - the everyday way locals drink it.

places.name: Single Quarters Kapana Market
places.note: Traditional brews sold beside the grills; ask the vendors for the fresh batch.

landmarks: Christuskirche (Christ Church)
A striking sandstone Lutheran church with Gothic and Art Nouveau flourishes, perched on a traffic circle and one of Windhoek's most photographed landmarks.
Alte Feste (Old Fort)
Namibia's oldest building, a whitewashed colonial-era fortress now housing museum exhibits that trace the country's history and independence struggle.
Tintenpalast (Ink Palace)
Namibia's elegant white parliament building, named for the reams of ink used in its founding documents, surrounded by manicured formal gardens.
Reiterdenkmal (Equestrian Monument)
A controversial colonial-era bronze horseman statue relocated to the Alte Feste, remaining a striking, much-discussed piece of Windhoek's visual history.
Independence Memorial Museum
A bold, glass-fronted modern museum shaped like a coffee pot, telling the story of Namibia's liberation struggle beside the historic Christuskirche.
Heroes' Acre
A grand hilltop national monument outside the city honoring Namibia's independence fighters, marked by a towering obelisk and eternal flame.
Post Street Mall Gibeon Meteorites
A pedestrian shopping street displaying a striking cluster of ancient Gibeon meteorites, remnants of the famous meteorite shower found across Namibia.
Zoo Park
A green downtown park built on the site of a former zoo, featuring a war memorial, palm-lined paths, and fossil dinosaur footprint displays.
Windhoek Railway Station
A charming 1912 German colonial-era station building, still in use today and home to the vintage TransNamib Railway Museum.
Katutura
A vibrant, historically significant township established during apartheid-era relocations, now known for its lively markets, murals, and cultural tours.

train.note: TransNamib's StarLine passenger trains (Windhoek-Swakopmund/Walvis Bay and Windhoek-Keetmanshoop) have been suspended since 2021 and are not expected to resume; see transnamib.com.na. There is no usable long-distance passenger rail - travel by bus.

bus.note: Intercape runs overnight coaches from Windhoek to Upington and Cape Town via the Ariamsvlei/Nakop border post (passport needed). Some services connect northward toward Victoria Falls.

ferry.note: Windhoek is inland. Namibia's coast (Walvis Bay) has no scheduled passenger ferry services.

half.name: Daan Viljoen Game Reserve
half.blurb: Daan Viljoen Game Reserve has hiking trails through hills with zebra, kudu and other plains game near Windhoek.

half.name: Okapuka Ranch
half.blurb: Okapuka Ranch is a private reserve north of Windhoek offering guided game drives and a lion enclosure.

half.name: Gross Barmen Hot Springs
half.blurb: Gross Barmen Hot Springs has a mineral-fed thermal pool complex near the town of Okahandja.
